body: Thanks for reporting this @PVergneau, I'll have a look at it.

@mkouba I made a quick test and I'm surprised to see that `InterceptorBindings#getInterceptorBindings` returns a `null` value in native mode while it does return the caching interceptor bindings in JVM mode. Is that expected? This means that the interceptor bindings are retrieved using reflection by the cache extension.

This is probably not related with the current issue but I'm curious about that difference. 😃

> This is probably not related with the current issue but I'm curious about that difference. smiley

Hm, that's not expected. Do you have a reproducer I can look at?

I had the same issue with my initial quick test. That's when I decided to add log entries in `quarkus-cache` and check what was happening. These entries showed me that `InterceptorBindings#getInterceptorBindings` returns `null` in native mode.

My previous comment was based on Quarkus `2.4.1.Final`.

Testing with `2.1.4.Final` produces a different outcome: the test won't throw an ERROR but it will fail because one of the caches wasn't cleared as described by @PVergneau.
It looks like there are two different issues here.
Yes we just saw that when trying to upgrade our Quarkus version. At least the first problem is blocked by the 2nd, preventing a bug in prod :)

The `IllegalArgumentException: duplicate element: @io.quarkus.cache.CacheInvalidateAll()` is a regression from `2.4.0.Final`. I don't know yet if the issue comes from Quarkus or a new GraalVM/Mandrel version.

`2.3.1.Final` produces the same outcome as `2.1.4.Final`.

> The `IllegalArgumentException: duplicate element: @io.quarkus.cache.CacheInvalidateAll()` is a regression from `2.4.0.Final`. I don't know yet if the issue comes from Quarkus or a new GraalVM/Mandrel version.

It's a Quarkus/ArC regression - we somehow overlooked the fact that `java.util.Set.of(E...)` throws an IAE if there are duplicate elements. I'll prepare a fix.

And BTW it works in the JVM because `javax.enterprise.util.AnnotationLiteral.equals(Object)` compares the members via reflection and we don't register the interceptor binding annotations for reflection.

issue.title: ArC - fix regression with repeatable interceptor bindings
issue.body:
- register all interceptor bindings for reflection so that
javax.enterprise.util.AnnotationLiteral.equals(Object) works in a native
image
- do not use java.util.Set#of(Object...) directly because it throws an
IAE if there are duplicate elements
- resolves #21174
